A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Autonomous Imagination work. Their main text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original counting, jigsaw puzzle, and object-placement experiments in Table 1, plus its own ROPE evaluation in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluations of o1, Molmo, and CogCoM, including numerical results and a qualitative failure case.

M1.justification: The focus/ignore/transform operators, cursor-control loop, segmentation algorithm, and scene representations remain unchanged. ROPE's rectangular-focus adaptation already appears in v1 Appendix A. V2 discloses supplied reasoning plans and prompts without establishing a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same counting images, four- and six-missing-piece puzzles, object-placement scenes, and ROPE subset. Moving ROPE from v1 Appendix A into the main text and dropping the IVRB name do not change coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds o1 and Molmo to the comparisons in Tables 1–2 and evaluates CogCoM on counting and jigsaw puzzles in Appendix A. The earlier GPT-4o, VCoT, sampling, cursor-only, and textual-CoT comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The new CogCoM experiment compares direct-answer prompting with explicit GROUNDING prompting. Existing sample counts, evaluation metrics, the 20-attempt puzzle limit, and the ROPE split remain unchanged. Newly disclosed system prompts and revised scores do not establish that the retained experiments were reconfigured.

E4.justification: V2 adds the CogCoM prompting comparison and a jigsaw failure case in Appendix A, alongside computational-cost analysis in Section 4.7. The cursor ablations, counting difficulty and reasoning-budget analyses, SmartEdit examples, and original hallucination cases already occur in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report counting-error means and variances without seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Revised variance values and additional result rows do not change the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises existing counting statistics: GPT-4o's mean error changes from 0.82 to 0.73 and variance from 1.49 to 0.62; the proposed method's mean error changes from 0.17 to 0.19. New results include Molmo's 86.2% counting success versus the retained 85.3% for the proposed method, additional ROPE comparators, and CogCoM's 30.3% versus 14.8% direct/GROUNDING success rates.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 retain the same probabilistic formulation and factorization. V2's visual-to-textual conversion discussion introduces no new formal definition, theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: V1 presents a general reasoning paradigm beyond clue finding and explicitly claims the IVRB benchmark as a contribution. V2 drops that named benchmark contribution and centers the paper on decomposing an atomic visual-to-textual conversion bottleneck that textual reasoning alone cannot overcome, while retaining the training-free closed-loop approach.

C2.justification: V2 develops the perceptual-bottleneck explanation across the paper, interprets counting performance as parity with specially trained Molmo, and suggests task mismatch explains CogCoM failures. Limitations shift from restricted operators and weaker-model applicability to proof-of-concept status, resource constraints, and the absence of native-model training and large general-benchmark validation.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds detailed task and operator prompts, and Section 3.2 explicitly discloses supplied reasoning plans. Section 4.7 adds SAM latency, RTX 4090 hardware, and average MLLM-call counts. However, v1 Appendix B.2's clarification that certain baselines are automatically supplied a puzzle piece is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially reframes prior visual-prompting methods around an unresolved conversion bottleneck and removes v1's benchmark-positioning subsection, including discussions and citations of MathVista, LogicVista, and numerous hallucination benchmarks. It adds Molmo, Tree of Thoughts, and Huang and Chang's reasoning survey; these changes go beyond citation formatting.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2 adds a problem-formulation subsection, integrates benchmark descriptions into Experiments, moves most appendix protocol explanations into the main text, and introduces a system-prompt appendix.

P2.justification: V2 changes the title/author layout and document typography, expands and reformats Tables 1–2, and relocates or resizes many figures. The main puzzle comparison changes from two rows to one; ROPE and failure displays move into the main text. Table 3 and Figures 9, 15, and 16 are new.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens comparison through o1, Molmo, and CogCoM and improves transparency through explicit prompts and computational-cost reporting. Its counting discussion appropriately acknowledges parity with Molmo. These gains outweigh the unexplained counting-statistic revisions and lost puzzle-input clarification, supporting a limited net improvement in validation and reproducibility.
